item.title: EU leaders gather in Dublin to debate who speaks for Europe in Ukraine talks
item.description: The debate, called at Italy's request, will not produce a name before December. Poland objects to western Europe negotiating over the east, while Estonia says the existing envoys are enough.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary moves to military base after death threats linked to Iran
item.description: The United States has also moved refuelling aircraft from a British air base to Germany and other locations, and charged three men accused of plotting an attack on another British base on behalf of Iran's Revolutionary Guard.

item.title: Slovak security firm links new email espionage tool to Russian hacking group Turla
item.description: ESET says the tool, found on a compromised Exchange server at a governmental organisation in Romania, was set to flag NATO and EU email traffic. A second victim in Kazakhstan was also identified.

item.title: US, Ukraine and Russia open first talks since February in Abu Dhabi
item.description: Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff mediate two days of talks on security guarantees and territory, while Russian officials keep European representatives out of the main negotiations.

item.title: Russia says no agreement for Europe to join Abu Dhabi talks with Ukraine and US
item.description: Grigory Karasin of the Federation Council dismissed France's plans to attend as wishful thinking on 9 November. Ursula von der Leyen says the European Union will still be represented alongside its partners.

item.title: Ten northern European nations sign pact to pool their naval forces against Russia
item.description: The agreement unites the countries of the Joint Expeditionary Force around the Royal Navy's plan to align doctrine, training and equipment across their fleets. The commander of the Royal Navy says the force will complement NATO.

item.title: Six reported dead and 16 wounded after man opens fire on Krakow's Main Market Square
item.description: Police overpowered the 24-year-old after a gun fight, and prosecutors say the same investigation covers three killings in his home town. Karol Nawrocki has declared two days of national mourning.

item.title: One Polish court now has two managements and neither has given way
item.description: A weekend order replaced the Constitutional Tribunal's leadership, but only two of the six judges elected by the Sejm have taken their oaths. The dispute over who controls the court will turn on those oaths and on whether any EU move goes beyond statements.

item.title: Nobody in Washington will pay for Europe's defence
item.description: The midterms confirm what was already true: Congress controls little that matters, earmarked money is intent rather than commitment, and the Pentagon is expected to hand Europe's defence to Europe. Member states should budget as if American money were not coming.

item.title: Dutch security report says AI now used at every stage of cyber attacks
item.description: The NCTV warns it is a matter of when, not whether, the Netherlands faces a society-disrupting incident, and names China, Russia, Iran and North Korea as threats.

item.title: Male State founder denies involvement in European flight bomb threats
item.description: Vladislav Pozdniakov said on Telegram that the far-right group no longer exists, as alerts again disrupted flights on 6 November. The Rome Prosecutor's Office has opened an investigation.

item.title: Hoax bomb threats ground or divert at least seven planes across Europe
item.description: Three of the affected flights were British, and one was escorted by the Italian Air Force. All alerts were later confirmed to be false alarms.

item.title: US to mediate Ukraine-Russia working-level talks in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November
item.description: Russia will send a delegation led by presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky, according to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, while European governments are unlikely to be at the table. The European Commission will host separate talks on Ukraine's post-war recovery in Brussels on 4 and 5 November.

item.title: EU adds 1,569 names to Russia sanctions list in what it calls largest round yet
item.description: The new listings, adopted by member states on 12 October, bring the total to nearly 4,600 and target companies at the heart of Russia's missile production. More measures are still being prepared.

item.title: Ukrainian firm builds 290-gram receiver that turns Russian drone signals into live video
item.description: The device from Kyiv company CODE380 tracks the frequency band used by Russia's Molniya drones since June 2026. Specialists caution its advantage may fade if Russia shifts fully to digital video.

item.title: EU adopts 22nd sanctions package against Russia after dropping two names
item.description: The bloc removed steel magnate Alisher Usmanov and banker Mikhail Fridman from the list after requests from France, Slovakia and Luxembourg. The new measures follow a harder line taken by Washington in September.

item.title: Poland's first Coalition of the Willing exercise in November, exact date still unset
item.description: The drill in southeastern Poland is to test command and logistics rather than show force, Le Monde reports, with airspace over Romania also included. Details are expected in early November.

item.title: North Korean hackers blamed for $6.3 billion theft from Binance
item.description: Trackers call it the largest cryptocurrency theft on record. Binance says it has replaced the stolen funds and froze about 2.7 billion dollars with partners.

item.title: Darmanin says a Mélenchon or Le Pen win would end the EU as it exists
item.description: The French minister warned at a Barcelona forum, weeks after both parties voted against France's 30.9 billion euro EU budget contribution.

item.title: Member states want more power over EU cyber rules than Brussels
item.description: The Irish Council Presidency has tabled a compromise proposal for the second Cybersecurity Act, as the European Parliament prepares to debate critical infrastructure protection on Wednesday.

item.title: EP delegation questions Hungary's rule of law progress after Budapest visit
item.description: Sophie Wilmès, who led the civil liberties mission from 26 to 28 October, said questions remain on the judiciary, corruption and media freedom, and no decision has been taken on closing the Article 7 procedure opened in 2018.

item.title: NATO diplomats fear US midterms will free Trump to cut European troops and funding
item.description: Pentagon officials are due to present options on the American military presence in Europe to Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on 6 November. Decision Desk HQ gives the Democrats a 78 percent chance of winning the House.

item.title: EU drops 'associate member' wording for Canada after German-led objection
item.description: The EU and Canada adopted a joint partnership declaration in Montreal covering trade, research and raw materials, but only after Berlin and several other capitals forced the contested term out of the text.

item.title: Hackers hit supermarket refrigeration in Belgium, Sweden, Estonia and the Netherlands
item.description: It is the second wave of attacks in three weeks, after incidents in France. No suspects have been identified, but food security is not currently threatened, says the EU's food commissioner.

item.title: Rubio denies nuclear strike on Iran is close after Carlson claim
item.description: The US Secretary of State said Trump had not decided on new strikes and preferred diplomacy, as Israel's UN ambassador also rejected the report. Trump said negotiations with Iran were going fine.

item.title: Dutch MP proposes law to ban addictive design on platforms
item.description: The Dutch Labour Party's Barbara Kathmann wants endless scrolling, autoplay videos and luring notifications classified as unfair commercial practices, with parliamentarians in seven other countries on board. Brussels has warned that diverging national rules risk fragmenting the single market.

item.title: Hackers hit Ukraine's air alert app, then Russia's EMERCOM app, with false attack warnings
item.description: Hitcore, a previously unknown group, says it targeted Ukraine's air alert app with fake alerts of radiation and missile launches. Officials in Kyiv and Moscow say the systems were taken offline, and Ukraine says no personal data was leaked.

item.title: Russia's exit from European anti-torture treaty takes effect, ending detention visits
item.description: The Council of Europe's anti-torture committee will no longer be able to inspect places of detention in Russia. Its president says independent monitoring inside the country has now ended.

item.title: Russia ordered back into ice hockey championships, several federations refuse
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport ruled on 30 October that the International Ice Hockey Federation must readmit Russian teams, but Sweden, Finland and Latvia say they will not play. The IIHF board meets on Monday with Russia as its main topic.

item.title: Russia lost territory in Ukraine for a second month running, US research group finds
item.description: Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy put the Russian toll in October at more than 54,000 killed or seriously wounded, the highest since the February 2022 invasion.
